clue.text: Silver found in lake in paltry quantity

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, describing something scanty, as the answer does

indicators.note: the silver is found sitting inside the lake, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a mere is a small lake
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A small amount of silver has been discovered in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or skimpy is available only in a small, inadequate amount.

clue.text: Neat expression of love, accepted by lots of people?

definitions.text: Neat expression of love, accepted by lots of people?

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: many people
neat and tidy means trim
love is nil, the letter O, as in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Wedlock is presented as a tidy declaration of affection that most people go along with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' is the container signal. Read as a whole, the clue also describes marriage: a neat public declaration of love that society accepts. 'expression of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is the formal union of a couple, a public pledge of affection widely embraced.

clue.text: cereal in a tub

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'cereal in a tub' (7) for APRICOT: the start is missing (no definition of the fruit), and the visible words do not build the answer; no reprint found.

clue.text: Thus to dominate unexpectedly giving lustre to hero

indicators.note: the letters fall into an unexpected new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Giving a hero some lustre is presented as a surprising route to dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges LUSTRE, TO and HERO into the four-three-five phrase; 'Thus' and 'giving' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the one in charge, like the cockerel who rules a henhouse, is to dominate.

clue.text: Groups of workers finding a trace of emerald in river

indicators.note: the trace of emerald goes inside the groups of workers

parts.note: gangs are teams of labourers

indicators.note: only a trace, the first letter, of the word emerald is used

explanation.surface: Teams of labourers find a speck of an emerald in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India.

clue.text: A marathon organised the wrong way in Sussex town

parts.note: a marathon is a long run

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word for organised is written backwards

parts.note: to have organised something is to have led it

explanation.surface: A marathon run in a Sussex town was badly organised, going the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns LED into DEL. Sussex is a county on England's south coast; ARUNDEL, with its castle, is in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a small historic castle town in West Sussex in southern England.

clue.text: Shoot round carrying a quantity of fertilising material

indicators.note: the outer pieces carry, that is hold within them, the single letter

parts.note: to shoot is to gun
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A shot fired round goes off carrying a load of fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts A inside GUN followed by O.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano, the droppings of seabirds and bats, is collected as a rich manure.

clue.text: Poet featured in series about writers

indicators.note: the series abbreviation goes about, around, the writers

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: A poet appears in a series of programmes about authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'featured in' is a link. 'writers' looks like poets, but it means pens.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan writer of the verse epic The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Covering that's hard, dry and warm

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to air laundry is to dry and warm it, as in an airing cupboard

explanation.surface: A coating is described as hard, dry and warm.
explanation.walkthrough: To air clothes, in British usage, is to finish drying them in a warm place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the growth that covers much of a mammal's body.

clue.text: Trailing in last, however you look at it?

explanation.surface: Coming in last place is accepted philosophically, whatever the viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase means coming behind everyone else, i.e. last; as an idiom it means 'nevertheless, when everything is considered'.

clue.text: Kind, allowing chap to lie in the shade

indicators.note: the chap is allowed to lie inside the shade, one piece within the other

parts.note: a shade of colour is a hue
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kind host lets a fellow lie down in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lie in' is the container signal; 'allowing' and 'the' are links. 'Kind' reads like a noun, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane treatment is compassionate and considerate, showing kindness.

clue.text: Original plot, expounded in opening chapters of long book?

definitions.text: Original plot, expounded in opening chapters of long book?

parts.words: Original plot, expounded in opening chapters of long book?
parts.note: a plot here is a piece of ground: the first one ever, described early in Genesis, the opening of the Bible

explanation.surface: It sounds like a literary critic describing the storyline set out at the start of a long novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a storyline, but it is a garden plot; the 'long book' is the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The paradise of Adam and Eve is the very first garden, described in the opening chapters of Genesis.

clue.text: Provide beastly weather?

parts.note: beastly reads literally as made of animals: weather that showers down pets, the idiom for a downpour

explanation.surface: It looks like a request to supply some foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pour heavily, here pictured literally as animals falling from the sky.

clue.text: Farm worker to assault woman's daughter

parts.note: to go at someone is to attack them
her is the possessive of a woman
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A farmhand attacks a woman's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends a flock of goats is a rural labourer.

clue.text: Composer utilising some double harmonies

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer makes use of a few doubled harmonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Composer utilising' as the definition; only 'Composer' defines, and 'utilising' is a link word joining it to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian writer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Henry's reign troubled with desire

parts.note: Hank is a familiar form of the name Henry

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of the word reign are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A King Henry's reign is in turmoil because of his longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges REIGN into ERING; 'with' is a link. Henry looks like a king, but gives his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A hankering is a yearning or longing for something.

clue.text: Extortionate demand that in another situation would make you yap?

parts.note: read the four-letter verb in the answer upwards, as the second word instructs, and its letters spell yap

explanation.surface: A shakedown demand that, in other circumstances, would set you barking.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's second word is an instruction: write PAY going up, as in a down entry, and it spells YAP; 'in another situation' notes this across answer would need to be a down one.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackmailer or racketeer orders a victim to hand over money.

clue.text: East European accepting bill for drinking

indicators.note: the East European accepts, takes inside, the bill

parts.note: a Pole comes from Poland in eastern Europe
a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: An Eastern European picks up the bar bill for the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is safe to drink, fit for drinking.

clue.text: Support sustaining individual explorer

indicators.note: the support sustains, holds up within itself, the individual

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A backer keeps a lone explorer going.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one who goes first into unknown territory, a trailblazer.

clue.text: Salve? Mention spreading half of it

indicators.note: the letters of the word mention are spread out and rearranged
half of the two-letter word it is just one letter, its second

explanation.surface: A remark about a salve says to spread half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges MENTION into OINTMEN, and half of 'it' supplies the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing cream or balm rubbed on the skin.

clue.text: Artist with strange, twisted, sick love

indicators.note: twisted says the word for strange is turned round, backwards

parts.note: rum is a British word for odd or strange
sick means ill
love is nil, the letter O, as in tennis scores

explanation.surface: A painter is described as having a weird, perverse and unhealthy love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns RUM (British slang for odd) into MUR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartolome Esteban Murillo was a Spanish Baroque painter from Seville.

clue.text: Greedily absorb assault, losing head?

indicators.note: the phrase for assault loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: to beat up is to assault

explanation.surface: Is a vicious attack that has lost its leader eaten up greedily?
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT UP loses its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf down or devour something is to consume it greedily.

clue.text: Feature of river edges required (just the edges)

indicators.note: only the edges, the first two and last two letters, of required are kept; its middle is dropped

explanation.surface: A riverbank feature is needed, but only along the margins.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep RE and ED from 'required' by dropping its middle QUIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses that grow along the banks of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: British in different ways causing trouble

parts.note: other as an adverb means otherwise or differently, as in 'could not act other than he did'

explanation.surface: A British person causes trouble in all sorts of ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link; OTHER is used in its adverb sense, otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is fuss, nuisance or difficulty, a mild form of trouble.

clue.text: State capital positioned with a river going round

indicators.note: a river goes round, encircles, the word for positioned

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
laid means put in position

explanation.surface: A state capital is placed with a river curving round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal and 'with' is a link. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital city of the Australian state of South Australia.

clue.text: Former partner to enquire about one's death

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: to enquire goes about, around, the single letter for one

parts.note: to pry is to enquire nosily
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: An ex-partner asks questions about someone's death.
explanation.definitionFit: Expiry is the end of something, and in older usage a person's passing away.

clue.text: Playing recording in excellent style?

parts.note: a show that is playing is on
a song is a recording

explanation.surface: A recording is playing, performed with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in top form is said to be working with great flair.
